messages:
rebecca.g: Quick Q — two things: 1) Is the promo eligibility window clear for transfers (IC->EM) that happened Jan 3? 2) If approved, can the effective date be retro to Jan 1 for payroll?

simon.p: Short answers: transfers are eligible if hire/transfer date was before the promo submission cutoff. For this cycle cutoff was 2024-12-31, so Jan 3 transfer would be outside standard window.

alexa: Oof — so that means the person who moved teams 1/3 can't be in the normal pool. Can we do an exception? Manager wants to include them, had expectations set.

simon.p: Exceptions possible but need manager evidence + EM/Comp sign-off + business rationale. Submit via the promo exception form. Link: https://redwood.example.com/internal/promo-exceptions (use the "exception" flow).

rebecca.g: What about backdated pay? Manager asked for retro to Jan 1 if approved. Payroll flagged that retro beyond X weeks is messy.

jordan.payroll: Retro pay rules: we can backdate up to 60 days without a special payroll run. >60 days requires off-cycle payroll and additional approvals (finance + legal). For Jan 1 -> today that's >60 days, so expect off-cycle. Also need the exact effective date in the submission and headcount coding (GL code).

mike-comp: From comp side — we need the promotion justification, updated role/level mapping, and an equity refresh note if this impacts grants. If it's an exception, label it 'promo-exception' and add the approvers list.

alexa: OK. What's the minimum evidence packet to make approval likely? Manager is worried about noise.

simon.p: Minimum: 1) performance summary (3 bullets) 2) scope change examples with dates 3) peer/skip feedback snippets 4) target new level and salary band justification. Paste into the form or attach a one-pager.

rebecca.g: Can you paste a tiny template I can use?

simon.p: Sure — small snippet you can copy:

```
Evidence packet (one-pager):
- Current role & start date: Senior IC, joined 2023-11-15
- Reason for promo: took ownership of X product area and led Y initiative (dates: 2023-11 to 2024-02)
- Impact metrics: reduced latency by 30%, shipped feature that increased MRR by $X
- Peer feedback: "Consistently exceeds expectations on cross-team projects"
- Proposed level & comp: Staff Engineer, target salary band 6 (range: $XXX–$YYY)
- Approvers: manager, director of eng, comp partner (mike-comp)
```

jordan.payroll: Also attach the headcount change req ID if this will create a new slot or backfill. That helps us with coding the retro.

rebecca.g: About backfill — if this promo moves someone internally and we hire a replacement, how do we ensure the new hire req doesn't block approvals? Manager wants hiring to start immediately.

simon.p: Start the backfill req with "internal movement pending" in the description and link the promo submission once approved. Use req template: HR > Hiring Ops > New Req. This signals recruiting to prioritize but mark that offer is contingent on promo finalization if it's an internal shuffle.

alexa: If we do exception + off-cycle pay, what's the timeline?

jordan.payroll: Timeline estimate: exception review (People Ops & Comp) = 3–7 business days; off-cycle payroll scheduling = next available off-cycle window (usually within 2–4 weeks) after approvals and submit to finance cutoffs.

mike-comp: I'll pre-review if you drop the packet here (DM or attach). Faster if we get clear impact metrics and a suggested salary target.

rebecca.g: Sending evidence in DM now. One tiny last Q: do employees see the 'exception' label or is it internal?

simon.p: Internal only — employees see the result (promo + effective date). We try to avoid wording confusion in offer letters.

hr-bot: Reminder: for exceptions include the field 'exception_reason' in the form and tag @mike-comp and @jordan.payroll in the approvers list.

rebecca.g: Thanks all — I'll submit the exception form and attach the packet. Will ping once submitted. :raised_hands:
